subject: Instructor grant: segmentation of free credits and eligibility exceptions
messages:

Subject: Instructor grant credit split + exceptions?

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the cohort loved the latency/profile examples, very compelling. One operational question came up from our teams that I wanted to surface before we get to SOW: we run an instructor grant program where ~20% of a cohort (mentors/instructors) get a small free-credit allocation separate from the core company credits. Historically we treat instructor credits as a separate bucket tied to instructor emails (not the company account).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood support splitting a single cohort allocation into two distinct credit buckets (company + instructor) while keeping usage and billing under one customer account?
- If so, are there any packaging/pricing exceptions required (e.g., different overage thresholds, separate expiration windows)? We occasionally ask for a one-off top-up for instructors during demo week — is there a partner/process for ad hoc issuance?

I attached the cohort roster and a rough schedule (codespring-cohort-roster.csv, credits_schedule_v2.pdf) so you can see the scale. We're planning to finalize commercial terms with procurement by Nov 10.

Appreciate any guidance — cc'ing our billing lead (on the roster) who may jump in.

Cheers,
Alice

Hi Alice — great question and thanks for the attachments. Short answer: we can support instructor-specific buckets and we have a few patterns customers use. Quick clarifying questions so we can propose the cleanest commercial flow:

1) Are instructor emails under the same email domain as the company (i.e., do instructors use company-managed addresses) or are they personal addresses?
2) Do you expect instructor usage to be active only during demo week (bursty) or over the entire 8-week cohort?
3) Do you need separate reporting/SLAs for instructor buckets, or is a single invoice with line-item breakdown sufficient?

Proposal options we can put in the SOW:
- Option A (single-account, internal buckets): Redwood issues two named credit buckets under the CodeSpring account — Company credits + Instructor credits. Line-item reporting and separate expiration windows are supported.
- Option B (instructor-managed allocations): We issue one prepaid pool and provide per-email prefix tokens for instructors; consumption is charged against the pool but we tag and report usage separately. No separate expiration unless we configure it.
- Ad hoc top-ups: We can provision one-off grants via our console (manual), or automate via an intake form + small PO. Either way we can include a commit for a fixed top-up allowance in the SOW to avoid manual approval delays.

I've looped in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (CS/ops) to draft the SOW language and quantify any discount/packaging exception. If you can answer the three questions above I'll push a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

Hi Alice / team — jumping in on pricing and ops. Laura's summary is accurate; below are concrete options and the commercial implications so procurement can evaluate quickly.

Pricing/packaging options (recommended):
1) Split buckets (recommended for bookkeeping)
   - Create two SKU line items on the invoice: CodeSpring Core Credits (prepaid) and Instructor Grants (prepaid, smallest denomination allowed is 1000 tokens).
   - Instructor grants expire in 90 days by default; we can stretch to 180 days with a 10% uplift on unit price (this is the packaging exception).

2) Single pool with tagging
   - Lower unit price (standard prepaid) with CSV-based tagging for instructors; reporting included. No separate expiration; easier to manage but less separation control.

Ad hoc top-ups / operational flow:
- For demo weeks, recommend a standing PO for "Instructor Top-Ups" (small monthly allowance, e.g., 10k tokens) that Redwood can draw from on request. If procurement won't sign a standing PO, we can accept email approvals under $2k per transaction and route to Marissa for Ops approval.

SOW language I will propose: 1) define instructor bucket SKU, 2) state expiration, 3) define top-up cadence and approval thresholds, 4) include reporting cadence (weekly during demo week).

Next steps: Laura / Alice — if you confirm whether instructors use company addresses and the expected usage pattern (burst vs steady), I will attach pricing examples and the draft SOW. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow if helpful.

—Ben
